past_medical_history: Focal epilepsy - right temporal, drug-resistant (2 breakthrough seizures/year)

patient.chief_complaint: Witnessed continuous focal seizure with secondary generalization lasting 15 minutes, not stopping
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Reyes is a 28-year-old Hispanic woman with drug-resistant right temporal focal epilepsy on dual AED therapy who is brought by ambulance after her roommate witnessed a focal seizure with secondary generalization that did not stop. The seizure began with left hand automatisms and head turning to the left, consistent with her known right temporal onset. After approximately 2 minutes the seizure secondarily generalized to bilateral tonic-clonic activity. The roommate called 911 when the seizure had not stopped after 5 minutes. By EMS arrival 8 minutes later, the seizure was still ongoing - now 13 minutes total. She was given midazolam 10 mg IM en route. On arrival to the ED she is still having subtle motor activity with impaired consciousness - 17 minutes total seizure duration. She has a documented phenytoin allergy (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) which critically limits second-line AED choices. She was adherent to her medications - both lamotrigine and levetiracetam levels should be assessed. She had been under significant stress from her graduate thesis defense scheduled for tomorrow. Sleep deprivation is a trigger for her seizures. The SJS allergy to phenytoin means fosphenytoin is absolutely contraindicated. Her escitalopram may have lowered seizure threshold (SSRI effect) and prolongs QTc.
